content.text:
Yes. The cleaned data already contains useful fields that the current scorer does not receive.

| Field | What it helps with | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| `person_core` | Titles and punctuation: “Sir Trevor Chinn” → “trevor chinn” | Still the same name evidence; it does not distinguish namesakes. |
| `name_accent_folded`, `name_tokens`, `name_token_key` | Accents, punctuation, and word-order variants | Sorted tokens can lose meaningful order. |
| `organisation_core` | “Example Limited” versus “Example Ltd” | Removing legal suffixes can collapse distinct organisations. |
| `alias_normalized`, `primary_name_normalized` | Explicit trading names: CSC Computer Sciences / DXC Technology | Use only aliases the source explicitly supplies. |
| `explicit_acronym`, `acronym_expansion_normalized` | ASLEF versus its full expansion | A generated acronym alone is weak evidence. |
| `donor_kind` | Prevents a known person matching a known organisation | A compatibility constraint, not a unique identifier. |
| `donor_company_number` | Strong organisation linkage | Already used for company anchors; unavailable for individuals. |

The name fields are defined in [funder_name.rs](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_name.rs:20). Existing examples are verified in [tests.rs](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_name/tests.rs:51), including explicit trading names and ASLEF. Personal title examples appear at [line 120](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_name/tests.rs:120).

Address improvements would particularly help the UNISON case. Current address normalization only folds Unicode, lowercases, and collapses whitespace. Structured house number, street, postcode, and abbreviation comparisons could recognize spelling variants while retaining disagreement evidence. Those would be **new derived fields**, rather than existing cleaned columns. See [declaration_cleaning.rs](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_cleaning.rs:173).

Member, declaration, register, source role, and parent-declaration links are available as context. They can help trace repeated reporting or select the correct payer, but do not establish that two separately named funders are one person. Payment parent references are retained in [input.rs](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs:25).

My recommendation: feed the existing richer name representations into one name comparison, improve address parsing, and use donor kind as a conflict check. Do not count several transformations of the same name as independent corroboration. For addressless individuals, these changes improve candidate finding and review; they do not supply independent identity evidence.

Two implementation constraints matter: the current scorer receives only name and address ([input.rs:192](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/input.rs:192)), and automatic linkage explicitly requires an exact normalized name and exact numbered-street address ([identity.rs:57](/private/tmp/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:57)). Expanding Splink inputs alone would therefore leave addressless individuals provisional under the current policy.
